text.text: Nice market with fresh produce, a deli and baked goods. I've only dined in once and have to say the top floor has a great view. You can also get coffee and check out the plants at the entry. For those that are new and checking out the deli, you order your food then take it to check out at the register. The soup and salad bar is self serve. The service is mediocre, depending on the individual staff. Some are more willing to smile and engage with customers while some are just rude and can't even seem to properly take an order. When you're providing service it's very detrimental for your business if you don't train your staff properly. The bakery has really tasty pastries and cookies. I would definitely go back to try other things on the deli menu despite the mediocre service, but I have explored and discovered lots of good local delis in the area and will take my business where they have good customer service versus some where with mediocre service. I would've given a five star review if service was better, but I feel the 4 star is already quite generous. My fish and chips were okay, the salt and vinegar fries were really good, and the club sandwich was good.

text.text:
La Fermière is my favorite yogurt company. They are a family-owned French yogurt company that has been around since 1952. They recently added a line of French Desserts. The Boise Co-op in Boise, is the only place in Southern Idaho that is carrying them. They have three of the five flavors. I’ve tried all three. I started with the one that I expected to be my least favorite, CRÈME CARAMEL, because I don’t particularly care for caramel. Surprise! Surprise! It turned out to be my favorite of three flavors. The Vanilla and Chocolate flavors are good, but they don’t begin to compare to the Caramel flavor. La Fermière’s CRÈME CARAMEL is one of the best things I’ve eaten in 2024!

French Crème Caramel is a vanilla custard that’s baked on top of a layer of caramelized sugar, served upside down with a caramel sauce pouring over the sides. It’s somewhat similar to Flan in flavor, but closer to a crème brûlée in texture. La Fermière’s Crème Caramel incorporates the caramelized sugar/caramel, into the vanilla custard.

The Boise Co-op in Boise also has the most flavors of La Fermière yogurt. The second best location is the Boise Co-op in Meridian, which has yogurt, but none of the desserts.

Highly Recommended!!!

P.S. I recommend calling the Boise Co-op to make sure this product is in stock before you go to pick some up.

Liqour laws DO NOT require scanning ID. Ask first, give your customers a choice or you may get sued. I will buy liquor elsewhere. Unfortunately I will buy less groceries as a result.

LOVE Central Co-op!!! Have moved too far away now and I really miss going for my stock-up shopping. The staff are fantastic and the store is welcoming and comfortable to shop. Great bulk sections incl. herbs/spices, oils/vinegars, tea & coffee beans (w/grinder available), soap/shampoo, local eggs & regular dry bulk. Also can do special orders of large amounts like cases.

I've come & gone from Seattle many times over 30+ years & shopped Central Co-op since before they moved & changed name. They're a block from the new rapid bus line & have free parking in their garage. Pretty easy spot to catch a Lyft too.

Thanks for all the great years & hope to be back soon ☺️🌈🐾

text.text:
Is there a store policy that prohibits cashiers from helping w/bagging? If so, please make it transparent.

Today I had bagged most of my stuff and had about 5 small items, such as a piece of ginger, left to bag when I had to pay. The cashier could have easily tossed those items in my bag while waiting for me to pay, but instead stared at me as I paid, very purposefully not helping.

I love Central Co-op, the produce and bulk sections are the best around, but these types of interactions really negatively impact my experience as a customer. And these type of instances have happened so many times to me at central co-op that I finally felt I should write a negative review.

Dear management, please make your bagging policies clear, since your staff doesn’t seem to help customers bag. And if your staff is so unhappy, maybe there is something wrong—are you paying them enough? Whatever is happening, it’s making me avoid shopping at a place that I would ordinarily love.

text.text:
DPA Application to Food Supply & Security Narratives

Context

The Somali piracy/insurgency analogy has been used to frame local food security disruptions as evidence of fragility in the U.S. domestic system. In this narrative, looting, shortages, or coercion in food distribution are equated with insurgent control over shipping lanes. This frame—if left unaddressed—can destabilise confidence in both government and private supply chains.

DPA Authority
•	The Defence Production Act (DPA) empowers the federal government to prioritise and direct private industry in the interest of national defence.
•	“National defence” under the DPA is not limited to military readiness—it includes critical infrastructure, disaster response, and food security.
•	Grocers, distributors, and logistics providers can be compelled to cooperate under DPA authority to ensure steady supply, prevent hoarding, and avoid private-sector practices that create unnecessary scarcity.

Strategic Rationale
•	Prevents insurgent narrative capture: By securing grocery supply chains under DPA authority, the U.S. avoids the perception that local conditions are deteriorating into “warlord economies.”
•	Undercuts adversary analogies: When shelves remain stocked and rationing is orderly, the Somali comparison collapses.
•	Limits liability for grocers: DPA provides legal cover for grocers who comply with federal directives, reducing the risk of civil or criminal suits for perceived discrimination or negligence.

Implementation Guidance
•	Federal designation of grocers as “essential infrastructure” under the DPA.
•	Coordinated requirements for minimum reserve stocks and controlled release in emergencies.
•	Clear messaging: “This is not martial law. It is supply chain stabilisation under federal authority.”
•	Partnership with local law enforcement and National Guard to protect grocer staff, while ensuring store personnel not explicitly assigned to security are shielded from liability and danger.

Outcome
•	Reframes food supply from a “Somali piracy” metaphor into a federally protected national security function.
•	Positions the state as proactive rather than reactive, reducing adversary leverage in narrative warfare.
•	Provides continuity of access to critical resources while avoiding escalation into civil rights or labour liability traps.

Located in the heart of Seattle, it combines a local vibe with a surprisingly wide selection of products. Whether you’re looking for fresh produce, international ingredients, or everyday essentials, this place has you covered.
The produce section is fresh and well-organized, with seasonal fruits and veggies. The meat and deli sections are also solid, with friendly staff who are happy to help with custom cuts or recommendations. One of the store's standout features is its variety of ethnic and specialty foods.
The store is clean, the layout is easy to navigate, and the checkout process is usually quick, even during busy hours. Prices can be a bit higher than big-box retailers, which is why it gets 4 stars instead of 5, but you’re paying for quality and convenience.

09/2022. Hey kids. I've got a brand-new update for you, and you're going to luv it. Behold the gentleman with the blue gloves and standing over various cuts of meat. That folks is Mr. Kenny Wilson. One of the excellent butchers working at the Hill Top Red Apple Store. What you may not know, is that he is the 'Yoda' for making small batch, non weird chemical sausage items. His specialty being...BRATWURST. Your thinking. Yeah, sure, I can get those anywhere. Well if you do think that, your missing out on what this master has been doing for this market for some time now. He makes that ancient and venerable meat product in recipe's you wouldn't think possible. Yet, he's busy at it about every two to three weeks, with something completely new. And every one is absolutely scrumptiously delicious. And that also includes Chicken or pork Italian sausage, plain, sweet and hot, and Chorizo! You KNOW you want it!
Just check the photo's for yourselves. So, if your just gaga about bratwurst that's non commercial and honestly made, you know where to go now.

text.text:
A Hidden Gem for Fresh, Customizable, and Health-Conscious Eats

My Fresh Basket is a fantastic find for anyone who values fresh, organic, and health-conscious grocery options. The store is packed with organic, gluten-free, dairy-free, and other specialty items, and the produce section was especially impressive—vibrant, well-stocked, and clearly fresh.

One of my favorite features was the poke-by-the-pound bar. We picked up 1.5 pounds of fresh salmon poke, sampling three different flavor profiles, and paired it with our choice of salads and vegetables to build our own poke bowls. Compared to a typical poke restaurant, this experience felt more customizable, more generous in portion size, and surprisingly more affordable. At $20 per pound, it’s not cheap, but considering the quality, freshness, and flexibility, it felt like a smart and satisfying choice—especially for a hungry lunch.

The atmosphere was clean, bright, and inviting, with a local and slightly cultural vibe in its design and layout. The staff were kind and helpful, which made the visit even better.

All in all, My Fresh Basket offers a refreshing alternative to eating out—fresh, flavorful, and designed to suit your preferences. I’ll definitely be coming back, especially for more poke!

text.text: I've been coming here for years and it's a great place if you're able bodied, independent, and already have a detailed store map embedded in your brain. If you're like me and don't know where stuff is and need some assistance bagging and carrying groceries due to a temporary disability, God help you. I've honestly started to question whether there's a CO leak wafting through the vents because every time I come in here the employees are wandering around like dazed sloths. I actually had a stocker glare at me today because I was apparently in his way; not once did he ask if I needed help finding anything, and I was too put off by his sour demeanor to ask. Also, the whole universal co-op thing around making customers bag their own groceries is beyond weird to me to begin with, but when an elderly person and a disabled person are back to back in your line and are both clearly struggling to bag their groceries, it's common decency to offer assistance. Instead, they just stare at you and act annoyed that the line is jammed up. The entitlement and snobbery here really sprinkles a nice dose of the infamous PNW freeze on the groceries. Makes everything taste better, I guess? I'm not sure what the deal is with the employees, but for a supposedly liberal, inclusive entity, I could not feel less welcome.

PCC however wins on variety against the LOCAL brick and mortar stores. The variety I'm speaking of is for organic, vegetarian, or vegan. However if you want Vegetarian or Vegan Lasagna, PCC will have several, whereas Safeway or Trader Joe's will have 1 to 2 options.

For me price wins Every time before variety and PCC prices are simply to high when the same times are cheaper within a 5 minute drive.

For me price wins Every time before variety and PCC prices are simply to high when the same times are cheaper within a 5 minute drive.

text.text:
Organic food-focused grocer in Greenlake. If you like Whole Foods, PCC is so much more pleasant to shop in, with fully stocked shelves and most everything you'd want to buy that is organic. I love my ice cream and the store's selection of brands and flavors is awesome.

There's a hot food bar and deli counters, and indoor/outdoor seating for eating in.

Hot tip: The store is a short walk away from Greenlake park (the playground and playfield side) so this store is a great spot to stop for a snack or a full meal.

I go I'm here just about everyday of the week. The staff are always friendly, even when I've taken my dog in with me on the recent really hot days. They live him here.

They have a really nice salad bar that they keep stocked up until 5 o'clock, which is nice. The ingredients are always fresh and the salad bar temperature is kept at the appropriate levels to keep the ingredients chilled.

The only thing I don't like about Ralph's are their prices. They are much too high. But much like Bayview, they tend to pride themselves on being an upscale specialty type of grocery store, who cater to the upper middle class kind of clientele who live closer to downtown Olympia. If the prices were a bit lower, they'd probably get 5 stars from me.

text.text:
Let me preface by saying this is a great store in downtown. They have a lot of quality products including groceries, clothing, kitchenware, and a solid wine selection. BUT they have some of the most unfriendly staff, I always feel like an unwelcome burden when I'm in their grocery and deli areas.

They have the BEST sandwiches (better than Pickles in both flavor and price) but even with the simple order form, I feel like I'm bothering the deli with my order (specifically, the two older women who work there), if the sandwiches weren't so good, I wouldn't bother just to avoid the brief but always unpleasant social interaction. They once even compared my presence to a fruit fly because I was waiting in the general area for a sandwich.

This review could easily be 5 stars, but with the sour attitudes I can't give that, which is disappointing.

text.text:
X Marks the Spot!

Ahoy, savvy shoppers! If you're in the mood for a retail adventure, set your sights on Star Store, the mercantile marvel that's more like a treasure hunt than a typical shopping spree.

First challenge: finding the entrance. This place is so cleverly concealed, you’ll feel like Indiana Jones deciphering clues to unearth hidden gems. Hint: follow the quirky signs, it’s all part of the adventure!

Once inside, prepare to be dazzled. The store is a labyrinth of eclectic finds, each aisle a new quest waiting to be conquered. From trinkets to artisanal crafts, you’ll discover treasures you didn’t even know you needed. It's like a Pinterest board exploded in the best way possible.

The staff? Absolute legends. They’re like your personal treasure maps, guiding you to the best finds with a wink and a smile. Got a question? They’ve got answers as golden as pirate loot.

The vibe? Think rustic charm meets whimsical wonderland. It’s cozy, quirky, and absolutely Instagram-worthy. Every corner is a new adventure, perfect for snapping pics that’ll make all your friends ask, Where on earth did you find that?!

In short, Star Store is a retail escapade that’s worth every twist and turn. So grab your treasure map (aka your sense of adventure) and dive into the mercantile magic. Trust me, the hunt is half the fun, and the finds are simply priceless. Happy hunting!

text.text:
Top of the Hill Market is the highlight of my week.  If you think shopping for produce, groceries, and meats is a chore, dread no more! The produce & meats are higher quality than I find in those massive, faceless grocery chains because Damu, Jackie, and the crew really do actually care and take pride in everything they provide.

The atmosphere of the place is even a breath of fresh air, especially when they bring out all of the produce, flowers, seedlings and starts in the spring!

It's not just customer service; they are genuinely happy to help you and know how your day is going. I look forward to seeing the gang and talk, it always leaves a smile on my face. I just wish I lived closer.

In a world where all of the grocery chains are becoming a faceless monopoly, and where food deserts are growing larger, it's nice to have this oasis of quality and friendliness.

text.text:
I visited Whrays Grocery Store recently and was deeply disturbed by the behavior of two employees. While shopping, I overheard them making openly racist and politically charged comments right in front of customers, myself included. It was uncomfortable and unsettling, especially since such discussions have no place in a professional setting.

As a customer, I expect to feel welcome and respected when I visit a store. It’s disheartening that Whrays allowed this kind of inappropriate behavior to occur without any intervention. I understand that people have personal views, but it’s crucial for employees, especially in public-facing roles, to maintain professionalism and avoid discussing sensitive, divisive topics in front of customers.

I sincerely hope that Whrays takes steps to ensure this doesn’t happen again.

text.text:
I’ve been a loyal customer here for nearly my entire adult life, but after my recent experience I won’t be coming back.

I purchased a 6-pack of beer, and immediately after getting home and taking it out of the bag, the bottom collapsed and beer spilled all over my garage. I went back to the store within 10 minutes, showed the employee the defective packaging and photos of the mess, but instead of speaking to me directly, the manager hid in her office and made her employee go back and forth. She then falsely claimed that “per Washington state law” they couldn’t do anything since the alcohol left the store. That is absolutely untrue.

When I later called the store manager, Steph, she was dismissive and rude, saying she couldn’t do anything but would “pass a note” to the owner. It’s now been two weeks and I’ve heard nothing.

Not only are the prices here higher than other stores, but the customer service is dishonest and unprofessional. Lying to a loyal customer to save a few bucks is the perfect example of stepping over a dollar to pick up a penny. They’ve lost a longtime customer over something that could have been easily resolved.

text.text: I have been so disappointed with Big Hollow the last several months. As someone who has a very restricted diet due to chronic illness, I rely on Big Hollow, and is the only place I shop. Lately, their shelves are empty, the produce section is abysmal, the freezers and broken and also empty. I already have a limited selection of foods I can eat, and when I go to the only alternative grocery in Laramie and everything is out for weeks at a time, I just don’t know … We really must be in a bad place in Laramie right now. Big Hollow- blink twice if you need help! Do we need to do a  fundraiser? What’s actually going on? Because as someone who is disabled and really needs Big Hollow to thrive here (I can’t drive out of town to get what I need), something needs to change.

text.text: I originally entered the Westland Fair plaza for a Walmart errand run. I had “turmeric soap” on my shopping list, but I doubted Walmart would carry it. There was a sign outside that read “we care for your health”, so I naturally assumed they would have the turmeric soap. It was a pretty busy shop and gave metaphysical vibes (loved that). text.text: Rio Market and Rio Bonito restaurant is a place which I go to every week. Their food is very good and so is their service. I recommend this place especially for Brazilian people that miss that authentic Brazilian food which is hard to find here outside of home. The quality here is very good, both at the restaurant and at the supermarket. My wife and I are able to find original Brazilian products that are made available to the Brazilian community in Astoria only because Rio Market exists. The food is fresh and well made, if there is any issue they will fix the problem and will provide very good customer service. This is a place that I come to for years and will continue to come to for years to come. If you do not know Brazilian food come to Rio Bonito to try it. You won't be dissapointed. Paulo.

NOTE: Vintage Grocers is located in the Trancas Shopping Plaza.

text.text:
⭐ 1 Star — 8 Years of Dedication Thrown Away Like Nothing
I gave Central Market 8 years of my life — showing up, working hard, and staying loyal even through some of the toughest times. I showed up after a tornado tore through the store. I worked through COVID as a part-time employee, doing whatever was needed, even when others wouldn’t. I stayed committed to both the company and the customers.

After all that, they fired me on my day off, not because of any wrongdoing on my part, but because a lead cursed me out by name, and somehow I ended up being the one let go. That’s how they treat loyal, long-term employees.

Despite always being told they “promote from within,” I watched them repeatedly give promotions to total strangers with little to no qualifications — all because someone put in a good word. Meanwhile, I was passed over again and again, no matter how hard I worked or how much I contributed.

The Grocery Manager, Lilly Lin, was one of the worst parts of the experience. She cursed in front of employees, told me to “tackle any customer that tries to steal candles” — and she made it clear she was serious. She also repeatedly referred to my kids as “gremlins,” which was incredibly disrespectful and unprofessional. No manager should ever talk to employees or their families like that.

The company’s treatment of employees of color is also deeply unfair. There’s a noticeable difference in how situations are handled, who gets opportunities, and who doesn’t. Customers at this store can be extremely rude and entitled — I’ve had customers yell at me, run up on me, and point their fingers in my face. And management’s response? Nothing. No support, no protection.

When customers gave compliments, it was brushed off as “that’s just your job,” with no real recognition. But when a conflict happens, they’ll turn their backs on you in an instant.

To be fired after 8 years of dedication, after everything I’ve done for this company, is outrageous. Central Market presents itself as a company that values its people — but behind the scenes, the way they treat their employees, especially long-term ones, tells a very different story.

text.text:
Central Market is undoubtedly one of the premier grocery stores you can visit, offering top-notch food quality. In my opinion, it surpasses Whole Foods in many aspects. The variety of products available is impressive, encompassing everything from coffee to liquor and vegetables to meat. Whether you’re looking for gourmet ingredients, specialty items, or everyday essentials, Central Market has it all.

One of the standout features of Central Market is its dedication to providing fresh, high-quality produce and products. The meat and seafood sections are particularly notable for their extensive selection and freshness. Additionally, the bakery and prepared foods sections offer an array of delicious options that cater to a wide range of tastes and dietary preferences.

Despite these strengths, there is one area where Central Market falls short: their kiosk payment system does not support contactless payment methods. This is surprising, given the store's otherwise modern and customer-friendly approach. In today’s tech-savvy world, contactless payments are not just a convenience but a necessity for many shoppers. The absence of this option can be an inconvenience, especially for those who prefer to use digital wallets or contactless cards for quicker, safer transactions.

Given Central Market’s commitment to providing a superior shopping experience, I believe they should invest in updating their point-of-sale (POS) systems to include contactless payment options. This upgrade would not only enhance the shopping experience but also align with the expectations of today’s consumers, ensuring that Central Market remains at the forefront of grocery retail excellence.

text.text:
I had heard glowing reviews about Central Market and was genuinely excited to experience it for myself. On my day off today at 8AM I drove 20 miles with high hopes, anticipating a standout grocery experience that matched its upscale reputation.

To be fair, the food quality and selection were impressive. The produce was fresh, and the variety throughout the store—from specialty items to bakery offerings—was clearly curated with care. However, the customer service fell disappointingly short.
From the moment I entered, not a single associate greeted me or offered a smile. When I asked questions in the produce section, the staff seemed disinterested and unfriendly. At the bakery, I stood waiting while the associate behind the counter failed to acknowledge me until I made it unavoidably clear I needed help. Checkout was no better—no greeting, no thank you, just a silent scan of my items.

For a store with premium pricing and a reputation for excellence, I expected a level of hospitality that matched the product quality. Unfortunately, the lack of warmth and attentiveness from the staff made the experience feel transactional and cold. I left wondering what all the hype was about. I will not be going back.

I decided to pay this store a visit because I haven't been in it since it was renovated and changed names. The looks are pleasing. Interesting color scheme. Black and Red. The store has everything you need for the most part. The only problem is the expense. Everything in here is a dollar or two more than other stores.

I feel like this store is strictly for the neighborhood people and the convenience. Years ago you could find a lot of cheap items in this store when it was Way field but I get it.

They now have specialty items and a better selection of some foods. They have a salad bar, hot food bar and a sandwich making station. I purchased and 8 piece smoke chicken and some bread pudding. The chicken was seasoned, tender and juicy. I paired it with a nice salad. The bread pudding was like home. Not overly sweet and the perfect consistency. I wished I had bought another one.

One other thing. Everybody in there speaks to you. They have a full staff and they are very friendly. That's what matters most these days. I will be sure to visit again.

On 4/5/25 Ellie, the Manager, quietly came up behind me while I was shopping and yelled at me that they were closed.  This really startled and freaked me out and she just stood there glaring at me and wouldn’t leave.  I had no other option but to go past her, as I was blocked off from any other exit, which I was not looking forward to.  She was hostile and angry for what reason I don’t know.   Then I began to walk towards her, as it was my only option, and she corrected herself and said we close in 5 minutes.   I continued walking towards the check out and she let two other people in the store as I was checking out.   I was shocked at this due to her anger towards me and that the store was “closed”.  I suddenly remembered my previous experience shopping there and that she was also very rude that day as well, although I don’t remember the exact reason for her previous rudeness, I definitely remembered her being very rude and unprofessional.
The store itself is great, no complaints but the Manager, Ellie…well let’s just say I am shocked she is a manager and even employed there.  She definitely has a negative impact on this business.  I hope the owners read this and speak with this woman who needs some help with people skills and customer service.

text.text: I’ve been an Erma’s customer for more than 15 years and have been so impressed with the staff and management’s knowledge, compassion and professionalism that I thought it was far past time to say so publicly. Everyone from Ellie (the manager for 16 of those years), Taryn, Ruben and all the rest of them have never once failed to  guide me productively and patiently even when I would have found fault with my approach based on being anxious about an issue or illness or  just being less than joy filled though hopefully that is perceived as rare! That is the truest testament I could give to the people who make this business shine and who have earned profound respect and admiration from me and so many of the rest of us. I know I am not alone in being deeply grateful for not only the huge selection of approaching “pharm grade” supplements at fair prices but the unending support this group of people who have served their community for so long and so well that I can speak to people in adjacent communities for miles around and have them share my love of the people who make this business the gem that it is for all of us!   (Sorry for the mushy parts Ellie/Taryn/Ruben…but it had to be said! We adore you!).

I usually enjoy coming here, but my recent experience at the ice cream area left a lot to be desired. The lady working the counter seemed completely uninterested in helping customers. She moved slowly, avoided eye contact, and acted like it was a chore to even take an order.

When she finally acknowledged me, there was no greeting or smile just a rushed, cold attitude that made the whole interaction uncomfortable. It felt like I was bothering her by simply ordering ice cream.

Customer service matters, even for something as simple as a scoop of ice cream. A little effort, a little courtesy, goes a long way. Unfortunately, this experience took away from what should’ve been a fun treat. Management should definitely address the lack of professionalism and motivation here.

During my recent visit to this store, I was quite disappointed with the service. Only two cashiers were open, and one of them was out of order. The remaining employee, a younger male, was engaged in a loud argument with his co-worker about how to fix the register, which was unprofessional and uncomfortable for all of us waiting in line.

To make matters worse, I was overcharged by $20 for two small pints of ice cream that were clearly marked at $2.70 each. It was a frustrating experience trying to sort that out amid the chaos.

Additionally, the overall cleanliness of the store was concerning; there were unpleasant odors lingering in the air and clutter scattered across the aisles. Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this location to others.

If you go up and down every aisle, it's like a trip around the world.

Customer service is okay, nothing outstanding and nothing bad. It's just okay. The cashiers get you out the door in an orderly way.

text.text: We were so excited to go buy up some stuff as we were heading out of St Louis.   The experience we met at this store was anything but that. Six years we've had to go places with a special needs child. And many times he'd be loud or whiny or that of a typical one year old or less. He is gdd along with multiple others conditions. People have come up and tried to help, or ask questions but never made fun of or insulted us as caregivers. Of course, I never even thought a store employee, owner would do this. For one, they'd lose business. At least ours anyhow. We had a cart full of things mostly not available at a regular grocery store.  Id guess at over two hundred at least . We also had another typical child with us . As we are in the checkout, one person in front of us , the employee yells " can you get control of him, he's acting like a baby" .  My response, " I wish we could, he's disabled" " sorry" . She responds again with crying actions and mocking faces telling us again how much of a baby he's being.  The child with us (7 year old sister) says very upset " he has autism" . My daughter picks him up and goes to car , telling me to do what I want with my stuff. She's already crying and as any mom would be , very upset her special needs son was being discriminated against in such a shocking way. I wait for the person in front of me to finish up, debating back and forth with getting the stuff we were excited to find, or walking out. I opted for the latter. I told the boys sister to put back her sweet find and she did. I very politely pushed my cart over out of the way of the other customer coming up behind me.  As I'm walking past the employee, she loudly asked do I not want the stuff. I say , yes , I did.  But not now after what you said to a disabled child. She then, and this one got me, asks me to put the items back. They were in the cart. And they were going to be bought. And we were next in line before she rudely verbally assaulted a special needs child. I don't think she'd if really wanted me staying in there any longer.   So, to future customers, buyer beware. You might get what you want with an extra dose of discrimination.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐ — Great Selection, But Room for Improvement

Jay International Food is one of my go-to spots for variety — you can find ingredients and products here that are hard to track down anywhere else in St. Louis. The international selection is truly impressive, and it’s the main reason I keep coming back.

That said, the store could use a little TLC. While I’ve noticed improvements over time, it would be even better with a deeper, more consistent clean. The staff gets the job done, but a bit more warmth and friendliness would go a long way toward making the shopping experience as inviting as the selection itself.

Bottom line: I’ll keep shopping here because the variety is unbeatable, but I’m hoping to see the atmosphere match the amazing products on the shelves.

Sevenanda Natural Foods Market — Atlanta, GA

I’ve been coming to Sevenanda for nearly 10 years, and it has always been a special place — from the incredible selection of holistic, vegan, and health products to the peaceful energy that fills the store.

But today was different. Today was extraordinary.

I had the pleasure of being helped by a woman named Shaina (I hope I’m spelling that right) — and she completely transformed my day. What started as a simple visit turned into one of the most genuine, uplifting exchanges I’ve had in a long time. She took her time to answer my questions, offered thoughtful suggestions, and made me feel truly seen and appreciated. Her professionalism, warmth, and grace are exactly what customer service should be. Whoever made her manager — kudos to you. She embodies what this company stands for.

Yes, the prices reflect the quality — and not everyone can always afford everything here — but when you receive that kind of service alongside that level of product excellence, it’s worth every penny.

If you want to treat yourself to something wholesome, intentional, and filled with good energy — do yourself a favor and shop at Sevenanda

text.text:
I visited Virginia Health Food Store today to purchase ingredients for elderberry syrup for my daughter, who was diagnosed with COVID-19 earlier this week and is still symptomatic. Out of caution, both my daughter and I wore medical-grade masks. When we arrived, I immediately informed the associate assisting me that my daughter was positive and still contagious, so she could decide whether to wear a mask or keep her distance. She was respectful, went to the back to get a mask, and came back to help me find the items I needed.

I was nearly finished shopping—about 7 to 10 minutes into my visit—when a manager named Celeste approached and told me I needed to leave the store due to concerns from other customers. I explained that I was only there to quickly get a few essential ingredients to care for my sick child, but she insisted I leave immediately. No curbside option was offered, no suggestion of an alternative—just a flat denial of service.

I had to call my mother and ask her to drive from Saraland to the store to finish the shopping. I waited outside for about 15 minutes, and even then, no one offered any form of assistance or accommodation. What made this situation worse is that the store was fairly busy with 10–15 other people inside—none of whom were wearing masks. There’s no guarantee that anyone else wasn’t asymptomatic or contagious, but because I was honest, proactive, and masked, I was singled out and dismissed.

When my mother came in to finish the purchase, she was rushed, and we later discovered that not all the ingredients I needed were included. This forced me to return not once, but two more times just to get everything. Despite the inconvenience and repeated trips, no one offered any form of compensation, apology, or even a discount for my time and trouble. The only person who showed genuine understanding and kindness was Alex, who assisted me during my third visit. After I told him this was my third trip back, he kindly gave me some extra elderberries at no charge, which I truly appreciated.

This experience left me feeling disrespected, dismissed, and discriminated against. I took every precaution I could. I was honest, masked, and simply trying to care for my sick child. Yet instead of being met with understanding or support, I was treated like an inconvenience.

Virginia Health Food Store is one of the few places in Mobile that offers raw, unprocessed herbs, so it’s deeply disappointing to be treated this way. I hope the store takes this as an opportunity to improve how they handle sensitive situations like this—with empathy, consistency, and basic human decency.

text.text:
I have been shopping here regularly for many years.  I was friends with Diane years ago, before the store moved.  I don't usually give negative reviews, but I feel somewhat bittersweet by my experience lately.  I want to love this store completely, because the selections are genuinely fantastic and the lower prices keep me coming back. Also, the produce, especially. in the last few months has been looking super fresh.  I did notice the new produce guy and he has been very professional and helpful.
However, lately often when I visit, I notice a very tense atmosphere. The employees seem to be efficient and do their jobs, but there's this palpable feeling of stress. Conversations with some of the staff are brief, tense, and everyone seems to keep their heads down. One Sunday I saw a lady, who seemed to be a manager belittling and mocking an employee right in front of me. It was very unprofessional. A few minutes later the employee was in tears. The general mood is more apprehensive than welcoming, which is odd since I know they're putting out great efforts.  I hope the ownership takes note and finds a way to cultivate a more supportive and positive environment.

text.text:
I always love picking up the ingredients I need at Diane's! I always head first to the produce section. So many good nutritious whole foods available. I even picked up Broccoli Sprouts this time!

I came in specifically for magnesium. I like to wander to the back left corner of the store where clearance items are kept. Sure enough, I found Magnesium + Calcium daily tablets at an almost $10 discount from its original shelf price. I'll take it! Even found biotin supplements at a discount too. There are all kinds of goodies in that corner marked down from their original price. Some visits what I discover in that clearance corner might be a hit-or-miss, but this time I found exactly what I was seeking at a great deal in my preferred health food store.

The prices are high compared to regular grocery stores--but understandably so. It is because the natural, organic, clean or vegan products and ingredients found in this store are worth the money. I prefer to treat my body and my family with only the best foods as often as I can. I wish I could go on a shopping spree here! Instead I just supplement my recipes with organic replacements if at all possible, and we can find here almost everything with need for juicing daily.

Thanks for existing, Diane's. You're just a hop, skip and a jump away here in St. Augustine. Cheers to good health!

text.text:
We've been longtime EarthFare customers, and in more than one state. Today, we were shopping in the meat department for "fresh" grass-fed ground beef and bought some.

Once home, we unwrapped it and found what you see in the attached photos—it looks like the "fresh" red meat had been wrapped around a core of old brownish-gray meat (which actually smelled). How else could the old meat be inside the new meat?

We opened the second package of meat this morning and found the same thing (see the additional 3 pics). This can't be by accident.

It seems the meat department needs serious remedial training in safety policies and health practices (at least). Customers could become ill if they didn't spot this before making hamburgers.

Very disappointing, to say the least, for a store that prides itself on organics, on product quality, and, from its own marketing, on a commitment to ethical management practices.

By the way, before posting this here, we went to the EarthFare website but could find no information for customers to contact the company or even provide feedback—apparently you're left dealing with a local store in person or by phone only, which is astounding in 2025.

P.S. I had to hit a single star instead of the zero (0) which was merited here.

text.text:
​Jungle Jim's: An Absolute Global Food Odyssey

​Jungle Jim's isn't a grocery store; it's a theme park for your taste buds, a genuinely jaw-dropping, world-spanning epic. If you think you've seen a large supermarket before, think again—Jungle Jim's redefines the concept of "massive."
​Even browsing during a work trip, this place was absolutely insane. Walking into the store is an overwhelming, joyful assault on the senses. The selection is the selection of the century—it feels less like shopping and more like an international expedition. The aisles stretch out so far that, as you said, you truly feel like you reach a different zip code moving from end to end. Honestly, Walmart is much smaller and far less exciting.
​The sheer volume of products is staggering. You could spend an hour just in the hot sauce section, which is a glorious, fiery maze of global heat. Beyond the essentials, the store is a treasure trove of niche items and 'nic-nacs'—you'll find international snacks, peculiar candies, specialty wines, and rare cheeses you didn't know existed but now absolutely must have.
​I think I managed to walk only about 60% of the store, and I was exhausted and exhilarated by the sheer scale of the place. Jungle Jim's is an absolute must-visit destination for anyone who loves food and adventure. Prepare for sensory overload and clear out your refrigerator before you go!

text.text: What an experience! This isn't just a grocery store! It is a destination. We only had about an hour and barely made it through a quarter of the store. When you walk in, it looks deceiving because the sections are walled off. If we knew what we were in for we wouldn't have spent so much time in the massive aisle of jigsaw puzzles! From the jungle sound effects at the entrance (the giraffe entrance that is. We didn't go through the hippo entrance) to the visible podcast booth, there is a surprise around every corner. There are goods from all over the world and many are authentic (I can speak for the Italian items, including Bialetti caffettiere) and their signage claims to have the cleanest bathrooms in Cincy! The aisles are plenty wide for wheelchairs though many upper items are out of reach.

text.text:
I had recently decided to go gluten- and dairy-free. I was having such a difficult time in the big chain stores finding items that qualified for both. While searching the web, Kindred Market came up. I hadn't been there before and happened to be driving by, so I decided to stop in. I was overwhelmed (in a good way) by all of the choices! I took my time in each aisle because the items they have there are MUCH different than you'd find at Kroger or Walmart. Many local options, bulk options, gluten-free, dairy-free, you name it.

I thought I'd died and gone to heaven when I saw their dairy-free section! I went in there with the idea that I'd only buy some dairy-free yogurt and came out with a full reusable bag. My only wish (with every place I run into) is that they would stock gluten-free Angel Hair Pasta. I can only find it on Amazon and in larger quantities than I wish to purchase.

I'll be shopping here for my gluten- and dairy-free items from now on!

ETA: 4/27/2025 - Kindred Market got in Banza Chickpea Angel Hair Pasta this past Wednesday, and I stopped in to grab some on Thursday.

Tonight, I made my spaghetti with the angel hair pasta, and I'm in absolute LOVE! Thank you so, so much, Kindred Market! You're so amazing!

I visited today and to be fair, I was wearing a long anime jacket and flower backpack at the spice jar section for a while. I was having difficultly understanding the amounts even with the instructions on the sign and felt slightly embarrassed to ask for more help/like I was doing it wrong. I have memory issues. I had multiple secret shoppers following me around which is totally fine, like I get it . College students likely steal from there all the time. So loss prevention has to do their job.
It did give me pretty bad anxiety when all 3 mean came to chat while I was checking out?
Some local places have to be expensive and I understand that, it costs a lot of money to import products like  they do. On the other hand, if you know what to buy from there it’s super cheap!!
I do love  kindred market and if I won a thousand, million, billion, dollars x3 I would buy from there everyday. I love kindred. Next time I come I will wear different clothing/leave backpack at the front of the store.

text.text: I used to come to Nature's Path when I was a teenager (almost 20 years ago). Now that I live 5 mins away, I have shopped here a few times. Employees are nice. Store is clean. And you can get some items you cant find at other stores. But majority of their items are sold at other stores. Everytime I come here, im really shocked by the prices. Publix is cheap compared to Natures Food Patch. They sell alot of the same items  you can find at Target, Walmart, Whole Goods and Publix. Here a couple pics of items. They're selling an Amys Margherita pizza for $14.79! Walmart sells it for $9.16, Whole Foods $10.59. Those Enjoy life chocolate chips are being sold for $10.99! I buy them from Target for $5.69. They had an 18 pack of pasture raised organic eggs for $20 dollars. They're about 12 at Whole Foods. Im not sure if they're having a hard time staying in business, why the huge price gouges. But its really unfortunate. Especially in this economy.

text.text:
I've been going to Rollin' Oats for probably 11 years or so now, and I'm so disappointed to know that Kim was let go. Her help in the supplements department was the majority of the reason I came.

I've been chronically ill since I had a massive allergic reaction in 2013, and Kim was listening to me before any doctor ever did. There are so many times where her recommendations were, quite literally, the reason I was able to still function. Specific example: my doctors ignored me for years when I expressed that my birth control was most likely creating a bunch of my health issues. Kim didn't. She got me to try evening primrose, and it was the only thing that got me through the days full of extreme body pain, emotional breakdowns in traffic, intense digestive issues, headaches, etc. Kim was right about it being a hormone balance issue, and gave me the validation that I needed. I finally found a doctor that listened, and she discontinued my birth control. So many of my issues cleared up almost immediately. It saved my life because it turns out that the style of birth control that I was on, combined with some of my other health issues, put me at an extremely high risk of stroke. It took 8 years to get a doctor to listen to me. Kim figured it out while I was on a shopping trip.

I was always able to trust that Kim knew what to recommend, and that she had my best interests at heart. It never felt like I was being sold the most expensive thing or dismissed. I don't think I ever asked her a question that she didn't know the answer to.

You lost a good one Rollin' Oats. I don't know what your reasoning was, but all I ever saw as as customer was a woman who cared, was very knowledgeable, and was worth waiting my turn to be helped in the aisles for.

This place has gone downhill fast. I am reconsidering my membership in light of fewer benefits for members, the last straw.

Having addressed other issues, such as correct food labelling, including gluten-free items in the bakery, hot bar, and take-home meals were met with defensiveness after painstaking attempts to address these via the General Manager, at Board Meetings, and also with the Member Engagement Committee. Even basic questions about where to place dirty trays was not resolved. (They do not fit in the bus tray.) The entire culture and tone towards me was shocking. This is no way to run a successful business and if your revenues are suffering, slashing member benefits is hardly the answer. By the way, I am a member of more than 10 years who has shopped almost exclusively at TRM and have visited several times a week. I hate that my feedback wasn't heeded and that I have had to resort to leaving a negative review, but it is a last-resort after going through all the other internal channels first.

This is not the way to run a business, especially not a cooperative.

Excellent store-made guac, almost no wait ever to get checked out, unlike at huge stores, but also more $$ than huge stores.    I wish they had labels for produce so you can actually see if you are buying cilantro vs. italian parsley, etc… also annoying- you have to look at tv screens to see prices for said produce, which is silly and non-intuitive, and just annoying.   But maybe most shoppers here don’t take price into consideration, but I don’t like the additional layer of hassle, not to mention who knows which sweet potatoes are organic and what others are by them when there are no labels?    Mostly very good store though!

text.text:
My spouse and I have both dined here as well as hosted a wedding event here. In both cases, the staff, atmosphere, and food were incredible.

Rachel, the Events Director, was phenomenal to work with in the lead up to our event (as was all the staff!) I could tell that our event going well was as important to her as it was to us, and she truly made us feel like family when it came to advising us on menu, music, decor, and run of show. While we did have our own planner, Rachel brought a lot of details to our attention that we wouldn't have otherwise thought of, so it really felt like we got lucky and had two amazing planners.

We also have a lot of non-drinkers and we wanted to serve an all vegetarian menu, so finding a venue that could accommodate our needs was super important - the drinks and food menu is so versatile and FtP made sure we were all fed and watered 💙

The night of the event itself was a dream and went so smoothly. The staff and kitchen made sure everything was tasty and served on time with our schedule. Our guests had an incredible time and we are actually still hearing compliments about the event, the venue, and the food over a month later.

We can't say enough good things about Rachel and her team, and we are forever grateful for such a special night!

text.text:
Came here for a late dinner close to the restaurant’s closing time. Our waitress was exceptionally kind and accommodating.

We ordered a variety of apps and the shaved kimchi beef for our main. For apps we got fries, ceviche, tzatziki, and an order of pita. Note that the tzatziki itself does not come with anything so you’ll need to order something else to dip.

The fries were nice and crispy. The ceviche was tasty as well, but felt the sweet potato was unnecessary. The tzatziki went well with the soft pita bread, and was quite large in portion.

The shaved kimchi beef felt like a more extravagant Korean chipotle bowl. All the flavors were tasty, but the dish itself was not quite what I was expecting. I’m not sure I would choose to pay $30 for it again.

I think we definitely over ordered and filled up quickly on the apps. Overall the quality of the ingredients felt very good and the produce tasted fresh. However, the flavors themselves were not something I’d write home about. I would consider Farm to People a solid restaurant if I had no other options nearby, but don’t see myself coming back.

I’ve been shopping here for about five years now, and it’s one of the best places for fresh, high-quality produce. Everything is high quality and locally sourced.

One of my favorites is their ice cream selection. They offer a wide variety of flavors from local producers, like Van Leeuwen and Jeni's.

The coop also regularly hosts local events like plant swaps, which is a fun and free way to get new  plants.

Most of the staff has been fantastic over the years — always friendly, helpful, and knowledgeable. That being said, recently an older Indian woman, who works as a manager or staff member, felt the need to follow me around the store. Yikes!!! This was a one-off incident though and I’m removing a star due to that experience.

text.text:
Fresh Direct Manhattan
Epic fail.  I have been buying from FreshDirect for years without very many poor incidences. However, this is the first time I have ordered in many months, and what a huge disappointment! I took pictures of the produce and bread last week when I received it to complain about the quality however, this week, I am adding to it due to the spoilage rate as well.

I was shocked by how filthy the celery and cilantro was and there was so much sand in the cilantro and so much dirt in the celery that it was clear the produce hadn’t even been given a perfunctory washdown.

The bagels and the sourdough bread were stale when I received them, so I ordered another loaf uncut the next day. However, those two bread products have since gone completely bad and moldy, see pictures attached. This tells me the product is either not being stored correctly or is being bought very late in the game and is already on the verge of spoilage by the time it’s delivered. That’s my personal take.

Of course I will go back to FreshDirect because i find them terribly convenient and overall this is my first terrible experience. but another experience like this would drive me away permanently.

Also, worth noting since they changed the bag styles to no longer have a cover flap and we were experiencing heavy rain, there was about a half an inch to an inch of water in the bottom of each bag. Not nice.

text.text:
So I ordered from these guys and they missed their promised delivery window by two hours and then (wish I was exaggerating here) half the order was missing. Then I called customer service and someone located abroad tells me sorry they can get me SOME of my missing items to me express and that will be there four hours later (makes you wonder how they define the word "express"). Plot twist: that express, emergency order arrives three hours late as well! You can not make up this level of incompetence.

Go ahead and search for reviews online. This is common with Fresh Direct. There is an entire subreddit dedicated to the chaos they cause in people's lives. The staff that work their call center must get paid handsomely because that level of curtness and blithe disinterest in your problems cannot come cheap.

And when the second half of my original order finally arrived? All the eggs were broken so I had to spend more time washing egg yolk off my vegetables and then calling customer service (again!) to beg to have the eggs refunded. Never ordering from these guys again.

text.text:
Really lovely food coop and community of folks. Rotating seasonal produce (root veggies, fruit, greens), bread (including good gluten-free options), plenty of pantry items (broth, pasta, oils/vinegars, etc.), household items (paper towels, detergent, etc.), bulk goods (nuts, grains, coffee, tea, etc.), and perishables (meat, dairy, vegan, frozen foods, etc.). When you become a member, you put in a few hours per month to keep prices low and it's also a nice way to meet folks and learn how everything works.

I've been a member for about a year and half and been very glad for it. If you're not a member, just stop by and ask about joining (can always look around and do a trial membership to see whether it fits your needs). You can then just stick with shopping and putting in your occasional hours or always get more involved too as you get more comfortable -- e.g., helping decide what to buy, attending meetings, etc.

text.text:
Kalustyan’s has been a wonderland of spices, herbs, teas, and more in Manhattan for ages. I’ve had the pleasure of shopping here on many occasions. I love being able to select more varieties of curry than anywhere else in the city. I already have hot Jamaican curry, this time I chose Trinidadian curry. There are varieties from a vast number of countries, each with their own unique flavor profile. In addition, I was able to find Chinese herbs of Anjelica Sinensis or Dong Quai (women’s ginseng), a pepper popular in Nepal, a variety of American bbq spices, dried and chilis, and so much more!

I noticed they carry rose water, orange blossom water, lavender, many natural hair care products, different coffee types ranging from those commonly found and used in America to more international varieties and favorites like Turkish coffee and the copper coffee pot. There are many baking products like differing levels of dutch cocoa powder, sugar - demerara, coconut sugar, many more kinds. A large array of flour types, sprinkles and dragees, including the De Ruijter variety beloved in The Netherlands for fairy bread.

You’ll find spices, herbs, ingredients, and sauces from all parts of the world. They also have some baklava and desserts near the register, even Dubai chocolate. In the back, there are many refrigerators and freezers with a variety of foods like Naan, Ras Malai, yogurts, meals, tapenades, olives, kefir, and so much more. Be sure to stop in if you’re in the neighborhood or visiting from abroad. This is a wonderful gem of a shop with many great options!

Really enjoyed the store, this being my first experience at a MOMs. Lets quick compare to other stores. It has that same ‘weave’ that places like Aldi utilize, where there is more of a winding, snaking central aisle with a perimeter. The produce is comparable to whole foods but smaller. The best part is the unique grab and go items like the Quinoa Tabouli- organic ingredients and low calorie but delicious. Many other grab and go items as well but no hot food bar or salad bar. That’d be my biggest recommendation for them. These are huge especially for business travelers (me)  or singles who don’t know how to cook or don’t have access to a kitchen.
There are some fun snacks that WFs and others don’t have so its worth the stop just for those!

text.text:
Debra’s Natural Gourmet is a hidden gem in West Concord. You come here if you are in need of stuff you cannot find at Whole Foods or a similar store. You can tell the love and passion of the people that work here. The store is known for the wide selection of organic goods, deli, and food you can eat there or takeaway.

I was on a mission to find a very specific vegan butter. Instead of winging it and going to the store (which would have been going to my fourth store to find this butter), I called and asked if they had it in stock. Fortunately, it was! Once I got in the store, an employee quickly assisted me and shared that it was a fantastic butter indeed. Upon walking through the rest of the store, there’s plenty of Walden Co. Meats, various organic fresh and canned vegetables, cheeses, and other grocery items.

Debra’s also has an assortment of vitamins, supplements, and prepared food. I would love to come here for lunch one day and check out the rest of the store!! She also hosts a variety of different events, such as making your own face cream, book discussion, and making bath bombs. If you also follow their Facebook page, you’ll get a heads up on Epic three day sales from Friday to Sunday.

text.text:
Dear Co-Op Management,

I am writing to express my deep disappointment with the treatment I received at your Hanover location today.

My husband and I were purchasing beer, and while he presented his U.S. driver’s license, I showed my valid Kazakhstani national ID, which includes an English translation and clearly states my date of birth. I am 26 years old, and I have never had issues using this ID elsewhere in the United States.

However, the cashier refused to accept my ID without any clear explanation. What made the experience especially upsetting was that she proceeded to address my husband instead of me — apologizing to him for “not wanting to lose her job because of us.” I was completely ignored during the interaction, as if I were not part of the conversation or not a full person.

This behavior felt humiliating, disrespectful, and discriminatory. I understand that employees must follow rules when verifying age for alcohol purchases, but this was not about the policy — it was about the attitude and the way I, as a foreign customer, was made to feel unwelcome.

I would like to know:
•	What forms of foreign ID are officially accepted at your stores?
•	How do you train your employees to handle situations involving international customers?

I hope you take this complaint seriously and review both your policies and employee conduct. I am open to further discussion if needed.

Sincerely,
Dameli

text.text:
UPDATE: this is why you need to do something about the flies in your baked goods cabinets... When flies land on food, they regurgitates digestive juices to liquefy the food into a liquid it can slurp up. They transmit microorganisms and pathogens from the waste and filth they've been on, potentially spreading diseases! Please stop making excuses and fix this!

While I’ve always found this place overpriced — even more than some spots in Midtown Manhattan — I’ve kept coming back because of the commitment to organic products, the community vibe, and the local sourcing, but I can no longer overlook an issue I’ve noticed (and mentioned) for a couple of years now.

The front baked goods display with croissants, cinnamon rolls, and other pastries is consistently covered in flies. Swarms. Crawling all over uncovered food. It’s not just unsanitary it’s a health hazard and it’s impossible to believe management isn’t aware, as it’s visible every time I visit.

This is a great place with great potential, but something is clearly being ignored. I honestly wonder if the health department has ever inspected this area.

Hawthorne Valley Farm Store: Please fix this. It’s unacceptable.

text.text:
The co-op is a wonderful place, but not a perfect place for everyone. They will admit that their prices are somewhat higher because the experience is better. There are some things that co-op does that they do better or only they do, there are some things that they are not as good at.

The produce is generally wonderful although a bit more expensive. Much of it is organic and much of it is local. The bulk section is like no other.  I’ve heard it said that it is the largest section like this in the northeast and I would not have trouble believing it. The assortment of nuts, trail mix, dried fruit, spices, maple syrup, etc., etc. that you can buy or as much or as little as you want is huge. It is hard to find a cheese section in the capitalist district with as much variety, or with the kind of service that will cut as much as as little as you want and they are extremely knowledgeable about cheese. The bakery is one of the few fully vegan bakeries in the capital District. They prepare wonderful meals and have a hot and cold salad and prepared food bar with a couple of different soups every day. there is just so much here that you won’t find in the price choppers and Hannaford‘s of the world. And, you do pay a bit more for it. The sale items tend to be really good on gourmet products. There is also a wonderful vibe with customers who will routinely say hello, let you go in front of them with your cart and the staff in general seems happy to be here. If you join for $100 you get a discount and if you work you get an increasing discount. Oh, and I didn’t mention all of the plantsin the nice weather. I can go on, but the co-op is more than just a grocery store it’s an experience.

People mention “hippies”, a “cult” and similar terms. No value judgement but a large part of the mission of the coop is to embrace inclusiveness of all….to embrace diversity and to promote social causes. The mission is also strongly supportive of respect and restoration of the environment, and this may attract shoppers and workers who are a subset of the population at large.

text.text:
I came in, one side is a small limited marked with wonder niche drinks and other such items, as well as fruit and vegetables, and the other side is a lovely restaurant and study space.  I loved the vibe felt so relaxing on the Market side. The restaurant ordering, she acted like I was lucky she took time out her busy day. But since she told me something was old, I thought, great she did me a solid, so maybe she is just tired. Then I heard the kitchen staff talking too. A bunch of hostile folks for no reason whatsoever! I bought my drinks on the market side, because it was cheaper that way.

I know, it was a Friday, and the week is long, but why you mad at me for ordering food? That is what this establishment is designed for. So my first thought was:
1. This food was not made with love. It will likely not be good.
I hate when I am right about things like this.

When somehow the spices are not ground fine enough, so one of your bowls you feel like you are eating gritty sand the entire meal that has the occasional flavor of beef and ginger, and lentils so salty I could not choke them down without rice, and even then could not eat them, that is how you know, maybe is not the hot spot after all. VERDICT: Hit the Market and only get the jerk chicken, rice and cabbage from the other side. Godspeed on this one.

text.text: While visiting Maine, we had heard about this gluten-free brewery in Portland, and we were blown away about how cool it really was in person. We came on a Friday afternoon, and there was a band playing, and the atmosphere was just very relaxed and happy. We enjoyed sitting outside and listening to the music and talking with others. We decided to come back the next day, and it was a slightly different atmosphere because it was a rainy day, but they opened up tables in the brewery room and it was very cozy and fun to listen to music again. text.text: I’ve shopped here as a non-member for over a year and took my time to review this space in order to give it a fair chance to impress or shift. The best part about this space: mini carts for your kids and a variety of selection when it comes to organic and natural items. The worst parts about this space: the products are insanely priced (if they want us to support local, they’re going to have to compete with Walgreens and Whole Foods at the VERY least), their bathroom is never cleaned, the farmer’s market (also local) is cheaper and has fresher product, and the employees have given me and my family some of the rudest (and most boring) customer service I’ve received in Portland. I do hope they change. I love what they care about but they go about it in what feels like all the wrong ways.

I was doing my normal grocery shopping for my grandmother and was denied service of her wine because my younger sister was with me.
He asked my ID and after I go to hand it to him he says "now can I see yours" while looking at ME and when I told him that was my ID he goes "well I need hers" looking at my sister, I tell him that she doesn't need to present her ID because she is 20
Now i instantly was confused as this hasn't been the first time that this specific cashier has served me with various family members including HER!! and he was sitting there  trying to ID my 20 year old sister who isn't paying, didn't load the groceries on to the cart and gave 0 indications that this bottle of WINE would be for anyone other than my grandmother. Let's remember I am 23 years old.. if we really use our brains here and think what 23 year old is drinking wine we'd come to realize that isn't a thing....
on top of this after asking for a manager the cashier proceeds to talk about me to the manager infront of my face saying things like "I'll tell you later" after whispering god knows what.

After being embarrassed and humiliated this cashier infront of everyone I simply let him know that I don't need any of my groceries and I'll take my business somewhere else to which this employee gets visibly red and upset and yells at us while we are walking away "thank you for your business" in the most rude bratty tone I have ever heard

So yea I did take my business elsewhere and I'm so thankful to say that the Clinton bushes has far beyond exceeded my expectations. Every employee was so kind, down the deli lady making us a fresh batch of coleslaw and  found us in the store to hand to us!! The cashier was extremely kind and followed the proper procedures and served ME with no issues safe to say that the extra 15 minute drive may be more worth it

This is extremely unfortunate and I'm extremely disappointed and shocked at how the cashier and manager Marcus treated me today. No employee of bushes should ever raise their voice.

Busch's Fresh Food Market on Sheldon Street in Plymouth, MI, is a family-owned grocery store that effectively blends modern retail style with traditional values and personal service.

Known for its wide selection of high-quality products, Busch's offers everything from specialty and gourmet foods to everyday essentials.

The store takes pride in its fresh produce, excellent meat and seafood, and a commendable selection of beer and wine.

Despite its slightly higher prices, many customers appreciate the store's focus on quality, freshness, and friendly service.

The store is also appreciated for its special hours for seniors and vulnerable populations.

Overall, Busch's Fresh Food Market is highly rated for its quality products and neighborhood charm.

text.text:
This store has a deli with fully cooked turkey for slicing, a slicer, and employees behind the counter. That’s all for show. When I tried to purchase a pound of sliced turkey from the Wauwatosa Outpost deli, their employee told me to go get a package of pre-sliced turkey from a refrigerated case across the aisle from the deli. I had already looked at those and they had been sliced two days prior. I told the employee I wanted fresh-cut slices, and instead of fulfilling my order, he gave the excuse that the pre-sliced packs were good for four days. That is when it became clear that I would have to go to another store to purchase that item. This wasn’t the first time over many years that an employee at this store had been unhelpful to me, but it will be the last time I provide that opportunity.

Reply to Outpost’s response: I reported this to the person working the service desk and he just said sorry. He wasn’t that sorry. I did contact the store manager by phone at 5:30 p.m. on Sept. 21, 2025, about this incident just a few minutes after it happened. He was disinterested. All I got was a “sorry about that” and “will look into it.” This business either does not care or it is staffed by people who do not care. It shows.

Brands like Woodford Reserve, Knob Creek, Uncle Nearest, and Hard Truth are available, making it a convenient stop if you’re already shopping for groceries.

The liquor section is separate and enclosed, so you have to purchase alcohol within that area. While it’s not a go-to spot for serious bourbon hunters, it’s always worth checking while you’re there—you might find a bottle or two worth picking up!

text.text:
This is an understandably popular place for healthy food.  It's a go-to for us.  My one complaint, and it's a major one, is that a place like this ought to be different from run of the mill grocery outlets when it comes to needing to be really careful.  You still need to pay close attention to the ingredients lists if you're looking to fight having chemicals in your food.

One example is rapeseed oil.  It's a cheap lubricant and somebody decided it would be great to add it to our food.  Problems?  Well, first the name, so they must have held a ceremony and renamed it to Canola oil.  Problem solved, right?  Ah... No.  It's toxic.  So, not to be deterred, they figured out a way to process it so they could get enough poison out to be able to feed it to us.  And good luck trying to find food without it. You can do it, but it takes a lot of work.

It would sure be nice to have an oasis of sorts where you didn't need to work so hard to avoid chemicals in your food.  You'd think this might be that sort of place, wouldn't you?  I'm hoping...

text.text: Good produce and gourmet food selection if you go there to shop but a disappointing employer. I would caution to anyone considering employment here to get your job offer in writing, take time to decide if it's right for you, and don't put all your eggs in one basket by committing to a role until you've actually worked in it and know that you will be doing the work/position agreed upon. After reading the poor employment experiences online and hearing stories about past employees in the store (not a single positive or kind thing) and noticing that no other employees seemed to work there very long, I asked for my offer in writing and then I sat down with an attorney to go over it. I would encourage anyone else receiving an offer to do the same. There are no formal internal HR policies (no HR at all so employees have no advocacy), no hiring process (interview, onboarding, training/support, etc.), no rewards structure or career ladder, and no benefits. There's no disciplinary structure either, and no job protection of any kind--regardless of whether it's full-time salaried or part-time hourly--so you can gather why no employees seem to ever be there. It is good starting pay, but that's about it. If you get a job, leave yourself a way out, and absolutely don't depend on it for your livelihood. Stand up for yourself to get lunches, breaks, and days off and to not be overworked. Seriously expect to not have a job the next day, no matter how hard you work or how well you do. originalText.text: Good produce and gourmet food selection if you go there to shop but a disappointing employer. I would caution to anyone considering employment here to get your job offer in writing, take time to decide if it's right for you, and don't put all your eggs in one basket by committing to a role until you've actually worked in it and know that you will be doing the work/position agreed upon. After reading the poor employment experiences online and hearing stories about past employees in the store (not a single positive or kind thing) and noticing that no other employees seemed to work there very long, I asked for my offer in writing and then I sat down with an attorney to go over it. I would encourage anyone else receiving an offer to do the same. There are no formal internal HR policies (no HR at all so employees have no advocacy), no hiring process (interview, onboarding, training/support, etc.), no rewards structure or career ladder, and no benefits. There's no disciplinary structure either, and no job protection of any kind--regardless of whether it's full-time salaried or part-time hourly--so you can gather why no employees seem to ever be there. It is good starting pay, but that's about it. If you get a job, leave yourself a way out, and absolutely don't depend on it for your livelihood. text.text:
EarthFare has a wonderful selection of organic and heirloom produce and artesian everything as well as bulk foods (which are hard to find) and very pleasant employees. They also revitalized a derilict shopping center's anchor store and gave the whole strip new life--major props for good citizenship.

The meat department has many organic and free range choices. The deli has things I haven't tasted elsewhere. The cheese corner is a delight, as is the young lady who (wo)man's  it. They have an impressive selection of craft beers in the cooler. Their prepared foods are also extensive and look delicious. They have sushi you can eat without trepidation and the excellent pre-cooked whole chicken is $5 daily. There is also a fresh juice bar.

As a very experienced bread and pie  baker, who became gluten intolerant late in life, the bakery makes me want to weep for joy. You should go crazy and try every kind of bread EF makes, such is the impression of what I've seen and smelled. The crackle of the fresh loaves is not something you can get outside NYC. I haven't seen bread like this short of my own kitchen.

As groceries go, EF is a little pricey, but what you get for the price is amazing selection and very high quality food given to you by people who actually seem kinda okay with their world, not *forcibly* cheery over top of personal misery (like at the big W).

Some things are worth paying for.

text.text: Best Bulk Bins! They have liquids such as honey, olive oil, & vinegar in bulk. Some comments say this is like Whole Foods or Fresh Market - I DISAGREE! The quality is much higher. Today was my first time in; the butcher told me that ALL their meat meets non-GMO, antibiotic free, cruelty free standards. They also have a "Food Boot List"; they boot "dirty" foods with 108 ingredients that are banned from their stores including artificial preservatives, MSG, trans-fats, Sodium Hexametaphosphate, & High Fructose Corn Syrup . (I checked out their website for this.) Earth Fare fills a serious whole in the market for people who want REAL FOOD in their bulk bins and not just a bunch of junk food. If you're environmentally conscious and don't want to purchase food in tons of one-time use plastic, Earth Fare seems to be a much better choice as their staff is accommodating; you can bring your own bags or jars to fill and they will tare off the weight. Their bulk bins have just about everything you need: several types of rice, flours, beans & nuts galore; best bulk in the area (I live in VA Beach, so I'm considering all of Hampton Roads). In addition, their organic fresh food is much better than WF or FM because Earth Fare has a good amount of Organic that's not wrapped in needless plastic. Yes, there is some needless plastic, but definitely less than at other grocery stores. For people who want CLEAN FOOD, Earth Fare is definitely filling a niche! I'm super glad to have a choice finally!!!!

While in line, I overheard this cashier speaking to an older caucasian male shopper about points you earn when you shop there to receive free items. No one ever mentioned this to me. So when this cashier processed my items, I kindly asked her about the points and if they could be added from the evening before because I had not heard of this. She replied, "uh, No". This cashier who so pleasantly described this program to the gentleman ahead of me suddenly became very rude. I was shocked and highly disappointed, but I simply and quietly said to her, I spent more than $450 here yesterday. No one mentioned this to me. text.text:
Mom's,
How do I love thee?
Let me count the ways!

Outside of the stellar customer service Mom's employees provide, what I love most about this organic market is that they are one of the few (if only) grocer in the DM(V) that sells Certified Humane meat from local farmers that go through a rigorous process to get the certification. I have become more conscious about the food I consume. While I'm no vegan, since I eat meat, I care about how the food I consume was handled and treated during it's incarnation (or lifetime).

Energy is energy. I don't care to consume anything from an animal that was not humanely treated. My temple deserves better. Mom's creates space in a competing market where we are flooded with food that is mishandled in various different ways with food that is handled humanely and with care and for that I am most grateful.

What I also love is how the store is always clean. I have never seen a spill in isle 9 that I had to notify management about. The produce is always beautifully presented. Everything is! It's a beautiful store to shop in and experience.

If you have questions about anything, an employee is always readily available to help. They don't go and send you to find whatever you're looking for yourself, they walk with you and oftentimes they will go get it themselves. That level of customer service anywhere is almost obsolete.

What I love most about Mom's is how they aren't just another business looking to exploit its customers with inflating prices for goods not worth their price tag, no. Mom's is an embedded member of the community and they act as such. Whether it's their recycling program or their pledge to their employees to provide a fair wage. They care and it is reflected in everything they do.

I really cannot say enough about Mom's. If I had to complain about anything, I'd say, I wish there were more of them. Do yourself a favor and shop Mom's today!

text.text: I absolutely LOVE Oragnic Food Depot! It's the best little hidden treasure for organic food in VA Beach! Whenever I need a few things and don't want the crowded normal grocery stores, you'll always find me roaming down  the aisles here. They have a small walk-in fridge in the back for fresh fruits & vegetables and other items that you'd normally find in the refrigerated section of a normal grocery store. I highly recommend them as not only is their food selection delicious, they have the most friendly and amazing staff! I've been shopping here since I moved to Hampton Roads 12 years ago, and I don't plan on stopping!
